verbatim: Three questions remain unanswered by the available reports. The recovery of benefit over time cannot be projected beyond the twelve months of post-trial observation, so whether any effect persists after that window is unknown. The relative contributions of the acute haemodynamic effect and of the chronic structural effect to the carry-over are not separable from the reported analyses, because the post-trial data include neither central eGFR measurements in all participants nor a randomized continuation. And the durability of the cardiovascular mortality result cannot be examined in isolation, since the active-phase comparison did not establish a cardiovascular mortality effect against which the whole-follow-up estimate could be compared.
whyItIsWrong: Gap section says twelve months of post-trial observation; results describe two years and separately report first- and second-year estimates.
note: Separate total observation duration from duration of demonstrable residual benefit; test year/month paraphrases without collapsing them. Keep the supported artifacts and calculations; correct or qualify the affected statement only. No human approval is required.
